findings.text: non-blocking: the calibration replay still computes its contradiction feature by ORing every answer whose key starts with 'check:claim_contradicts_source:', so once receipts are recorded with the new per-binding keys one contradicting binding marks the claim contradicted, while aggregate_docs_review on the same row folds by support; a refit through _docs_axis would then measure the retired per-source semantics. The file was held by sib-red-product-defects and correctly left untouched, so this needs a follow-up there (or a fold helper the calibration can call).

non-blocking: docs_binding_ids labels bindings from the raw item['dd_source_docs'] while the evidence the judge reads is comparison_sources(...) at :824, so the position-to-binding alignment the per-binding questions rely on (the prompt names dd_source_docs.value[position] as the definition of binding position) holds only because comparison_sources happens never to drop an entry; a filter added there would silently attribute each reading to the wrong DD definition. Deriving the labels from the same transformed list would make the alignment structural.

non-blocking: ELECTROSTATIC_SCOPE and S0010_DOCUMENTATION are constructed texts that restate the recorded cases rather than the documentation those names actually carry, so the fixtures pin the fold's behaviour on a faithful pastiche and would not catch a regression that only misfires on the real sentences (sentence splitting, registry-sentence stripping, or a scope sentence phrased differently).

non-blocking: binding_labels is built straight from state['binding_ids'], where the per-source code it replaced applied strip_dd_prefix to the same ids at :682 and :694; a hold message now records whichever id form dd_source_docs carries, so the same binding can appear unprefixed in a new note and prefixed in an older one.
